content.title: Big Prometheus at Scale: Pros, Cons, and a MoSCoW Map of Observability Tools
content.sub_title: TenthMatrix rewrite of the Big Prometheus problem space: Thanos, Cortex/Mimir, VictoriaMetrics, M3/Chronosphere — plus MoSCoW across OTEL, Grafana, SaaS APM and more
content.content:
TenthMatrix technical rewrite and expansion of the “Big Prometheus” problem space popularised by Clay Smith’s Monitoring Monitoring essay (Thanos, Cortex, M3DB, VictoriaMetrics). This article adds sharper pros/cons, a MoSCoW analysis across many observability tools, and a recommendation path for Kubernetes-native estates. Companion for managers: Observability is a business standard.

Thesis. Prometheus-per-cluster is the right local unit — and a terrible global product. “Big Prometheus” projects exist to restore global query, long-term retention, and HA without abandoning PromQL. Pick them only when scale forces you to; always pick a company-wide observability standard first. People in the know still say: think carefully before you run a hyperscale metrics database you do not need.

1. The problem Big Prometheus solves

Large organisations accumulate specialised stacks for dashboarding, embedded stats, time-series monitoring, and ad-hoc analysis. That creates silos of data and processing — complex, expensive, and hard to maintain. In Kubernetes land the de facto open-source metrics unit is Prometheus (usually with Grafana and Alertmanager). A common pattern is one Prometheus per cluster via Prometheus Operator / kube-prometheus-stack.

At tens or hundreds of clusters, local Prometheus is no longer enough:

  • Global questions (“which clusters are on fire?”) become slow or impossible.
  • Retention on every Prometheus disk becomes costly and inconsistent.
  • HA and durable history need a deliberate store, not “bigger PVC.”

Four major open-source lineages addressed that gap: Thanos, Cortex (and today’s Grafana Mimir), M3DB (and Chronosphere), and VictoriaMetrics. Shared goals: Prometheus compatibility, global fast queries, long-term cheap(er) history, and high availability.

2. Option deep dive — pros and cons that matter

2.1 Thanos

Model: Keep Prometheus closer to the default — sidecars or receive path; query globally; ship blocks to object storage (S3/GCS/Azure).

Pros

  • Fits existing Prometheus-per-cluster mental model.
  • Object storage for long-term history is usually cheaper than always-hot NoSQL.
  • Strong CNCF / community gravity; many production war stories.
  • Compactor + downsampling help control cost at age.

Cons

  • Global query fan-out can be latency-sensitive; store-gateway tuning matters.
  • Operational surface (sidecar, querier, store, compactor, ruler) is real.
  • Object-store GET patterns can surprise on bandwidth bills if mis-tuned.

Choose when: You already run many Prometheuses and want global query without a full rewrite of the write path.

2.2 Cortex → Grafana Mimir

Model: SaaS-like central store. Clusters remote_write into a multi-tenant metrics platform. Cortex pioneered this; Grafana Mimir is the modern production-hardened lineage most teams evaluate now.

Pros

  • Multi-tenancy and central ownership match a platform-team org chart.
  • Familiar to anyone buying Grafana Cloud / running Grafana LGTM.
  • Object-store backends are first-class in modern deployments.
  • Strong path for recording rules and alert evaluation at the centre.

Cons

  • Write-path and ingester/compactor ops are non-trivial at scale.
  • Misconfigured remote_write or cardinality can melt the central cluster.
  • “Just enable remote_write” without budgets is an expensive hobby.

Choose when: A central observability platform team will own the metrics fabric for many product teams.

2.3 VictoriaMetrics

Model: PromQL-compatible TSDB with a reputation for compression and simpler ops; single-node for small estates, clustered for larger; commercial cloud available.

Pros

  • Often excellent cost/performance for self-hosted metrics.
  • Operational simplicity relative to full Thanos/Mimir meshes.
  • Clear upgrade path from single node to cluster.
  • Good fit when FinOps pressure is the primary constraint.

Cons

  • Smaller “default CNCF” mindshare than Thanos/Mimir in some ecosystems.
  • You still need Grafana, Alertmanager, and an OTEL story around it.
  • Vendor cloud vs OSS split needs a clear procurement stance.

Choose when: You want PromQL scale with fewer moving parts and aggressive storage efficiency.

2.4 M3DB / Chronosphere

Model: Uber-born stack optimised for huge cardinality and hot historical reads; Chronosphere commercialises the operational path.

Pros

  • Proven at extreme scale where object-store-only history was too slow or too pricey across cloud/on-prem boundaries.
  • Commercial offering reduces DIY distributed-systems burden.

Cons

  • Complexity and specialisation — easy to over-buy.
  • OSS vs SaaS strategy must be explicit.
  • Most companies should not start here.

Choose when: Cardinality and historical query patterns have already broken cheaper architectures — or you deliberately buy Chronosphere.

Caution (still true). Do not adopt Thanos/Mimir/VM/M3 because a blog post listed them. Adopt them when global query, retention cost, or HA requirements are measured pains. Until then: solid Prometheus Operator, recording rules, Alertmanager, Grafana, and OpenTelemetry will carry most businesses.

3. MoSCoW analysis of the observability tool landscape

Scope: a Kubernetes-native product company standardising observability across many services (including AI agents). MoSCoW is for the standard, not a shopping list to install on day one.

Tool / capability MoSCoW Role in the standard Notes
OpenTelemetryMustVendor-neutral telemetry contractSDKs + Collector; refuse proprietary-only emitters
PrometheusMustPer-cluster metrics unitOperator / kube-prometheus-stack
GrafanaMustShared visualisationFolder + datasource governance
AlertmanagerMustAlert routing / silencePair with PagerDuty/Opsgenie/etc.
Logs (Loki or ELK/OpenSearch)MustCentral structured logsPick one primary; ban log-in-Slack
Traces (Tempo / Jaeger)MustDistributed tracing storeSampling policy required
Fluent Bit / VectorMustLog/ship agentsPrefer one agent family
Thanos / Mimir / VictoriaMetricsShouldGlobal + long-term metricsWhen multi-cluster pain is real
Recording rules + cardinality budgetsShouldCost and query hygieneEnforce in CI / admission
Blackbox / syntheticsShouldUser-path probesCritical journeys only first
Sentry-class errorsShouldException intelligenceLink to traces via IDs
Pyroscope / profilingShouldContinuous profilingCPU/mem hotspots in prod
Langfuse / LLM observabilityShould*Agent/LLM spans & cost*Must if you ship AI agents
Datadog / New Relic / DynatraceCouldFull SaaS APMOK if OTEL export + FinOps caps
Chronosphere / M3 pathCouldHyperscale metrics SaaS/OSSBuy when scale justifies
eBPF auto-platformsCouldLow-touch signalsSupplement, don’t replace SLOs
RUM / session replayCouldFront-end experiencePrivacy review required
Per-team proprietary APM w/ no exportWon’tBreaks the standardCreates unmergeable truths
Unlimited cardinality / raw everythingWon’tBudget killerPolicy + CI gates
Optional prod monitoringWon’tGovernance failureRelease blocker instead

4. Reference architecture (TenthMatrix-shaped)

  1. Emit — Apps and agents use OpenTelemetry; metrics also expose Prometheus endpoints where natural.
  2. Collect — OTEL Collector + Prometheus scrape; Fluent Bit/Vector for logs.
  3. Store local — Prometheus per cluster (short retention) for independence.
  4. Store global — Thanos or Mimir or VictoriaMetrics when multi-cluster query/retention demands it.
  5. Correlate — Grafana explores metrics + Loki/ELK logs + Tempo/Jaeger traces with shared trace IDs.
  6. Act — Alertmanager → on-call; SLOs on golden journeys (checkout, agent reply, edge 5xx).
  7. Govern — Cardinality budgets, sampling, retention classes (hot/warm/cold), access control, audit.

5. When SaaS is the right “Big Prometheus”

Paying Datadog, Grafana Cloud, Chronosphere, New Relic, or Dynatrace is often rational: you are buying an ops team and a multi-tenant store. The standard still applies — insist on OpenTelemetry instrumentation, exportability, and cost controls. Many SaaS backends are themselves descendants of Cortex/Mimir/Thanos-class thinking. Buying does not excuse siloed optional monitoring.

6. Decision checklist

  • Do we have a written observability standard (Must/Should/Could/Won’t)?
  • Can we answer global health questions without five UIs?
  • Is production release blocked without golden signals?
  • Do we know monthly telemetry cost and top cardinality offenders?
  • Have we measured the pain that justifies Thanos/Mimir/VM/M3 — or are we fashion-shopping?

7. Related TenthMatrix reading

  • Manager blog — observability as a business standard
  • LLM bottlenecks, OpenTelemetry, and cost control · technical brief
  • Ring Promoter — every release earns production (promotion health pairs with observability)
  • Source inspiration: Big Prometheus — Monitoring Monitoring (Clay Smith, 2020)

content.title: WSL Vault Technical Deep Dive: Zero-Trust Secrets, Dual Control, MFA & Multi-Region HA
content.sub_title: Technical deep dive: envelope hierarchy, dual-control workflows, MFA, leases, active/active multi-region HA, feature tours, and presentation chapters
content.content:
Long-form technical companion to the compliance blog. How WSL Vault makes secret management a breeze for operators while enforcing cryptographic tenant isolation, dual-control shared access, MFA, dynamic leases, and active/active multi-region HA. Product: TenthMatrix WSL Vault · wslvault.org · GitHub.

Presentation (~20 min) — youtu.be/O6q3_H0k2M8 · Silent tour: wslvault.org/#tour

Thesis. A secrets platform is only “easy” if the safe path is the fast path — and only trustworthy if one compromised credential cannot empty the building. WSL Vault combines Vault-compatible engines with a per-tenant envelope hierarchy, MFA-backed identity, real leases, and active/active regions so operators move quickly while blast radius stays one tenant wide.

1. Why shared root power fails audits

In many HashiCorp Vault deployments, a root token (or equivalent highly privileged unseal/admin path) remains the organisational backstop. That credential’s blast radius is the entire secrets graph: every namespace, every environment, every team’s API keys and database passwords. If it lands in the wrong hands, you do not have an incident ticket — you have a breach narrative.

WSL Vault’s answer is structural: identity is a signed, per-tenant token; material is sealed under a tenant KEK; cross-tenant requests fail closed at the crypto layer. Root custody, when needed for unseal, can be Shamir-split so no single operator holds the whole key.

2. Envelope encryption — the reason isolation is real

Each secret is sealed with a data encryption key (DEK). The DEK is wrapped under a tenant KEK. Tenant KEKs are wrapped under a root KEK held by the crypto service (KMS, HSM, or Shamir quorum). AES-256-GCM provides authenticated encryption. A database dump yields ciphertext wrapped under keys the database never sees.

That is why “steal the server” does not equal “steal the secrets” — and why Team A’s token cannot unwrap Team B’s DEKs even if an upper layer mislabels a path.

3. Tenants for apps, teams, and environments

Model the organisation the way auditors already think:

  • App tenants — Shop vs OpsAPI vs edge proxies each keep separate sealed material.
  • Team tenants — Platform, payments, data science never share unwrap rights by accident.
  • Environment tenants — INT / TEST / ACC / PROD as separate crypto worlds so a staging token cannot open production.

Isolation is not a WHERE clause. A cross-tenant read returns not found. That cryptographic refusal is what you show in a control description.

4. Ceremony workflow — oath and dual-tenant control

  1. Issue — At ceremony close, each tenant custodian receives a signed per-tenant token (and MFA enrolment).
  2. Oath — Custodians accept personal responsibility: never share the token, never store it in chat or git, rotate on departure.
  3. Day-to-day — Team A operates only inside Tenant A. Sprawl drops because the vault is the fastest place to put a secret.
  4. Wide audience / shared path — For secrets that must be obtained across tenants (joint release, shared break-glass, dual approval), policy requires both Tenant A and Tenant B tokens (plus MFA). Neither side alone succeeds.
  5. Audit — Both presentations and the stated purpose land on the per-tenant hash chain.

That dual-control gate is how you translate zero trust into an operating procedure regulators recognise.

5. Making secrets a breeze — engines and workflows

Feature tour (aligned with wslvault.org/#features):

Surface Operator experience Security property
KV v2Versioned put/get, check-and-set, soft-delete/destroySealed before disk under tenant hierarchy
TransitEncrypt / decrypt / sign / verify in one callPlaintext keys never leave the vault
PKIPrivate CA, roles, short-lived certsCA keys envelope-encrypted
LeasesIssue, renew, list, revokeRevoke stops use immediately
Identity + MFATOTP, recovery codes, OIDC/LDAP/mTLS/workloadSigned per-tenant token — never a trusted header alone
 
$ wslvault login --key wslv_…
✓ authenticated as tenant payments  region=manchester  mfa=ok

$ wslvault kv put prod/db/creds password=••••
✓ sealed with dek 01a0…93a7  version=1

$ wslvault kv get prod/db/creds --region london
# same secret, peer region decrypt
password = ••••   replication_lag=14ms

$ wslvault lease revoke lease_…
✓ credential dead — not a soft flag

6. MFA and identity detail

Humans enrol self-service TOTP with recovery codes. API keys and JWTs sit under fine-grained policies. Workloads authenticate with mTLS or cloud-workload patterns so apps never borrow a human root. Identity always resolves to a tenant-scoped principal before any unwrap.

That combination — MFA for people, short leases for machines — is what keeps “convenient” from becoming “copied into a wiki.”

7. Multi-region HA without a shared live database

Each region is a complete stack: own PostgreSQL, own services, own public hostname. Regions share key material, not one hot database. Agents pull encrypted changes over the public edge. Clients read the same sealed secret from the peer with low replication lag. Failover is a PoP / traffic decision — operators do not rebuild custody under pressure.

Every operation joins a per-tenant signed hash chain. Records cannot be silently altered without breaking the chain — the evidence pack auditors ask for.

8. Deploy path — Kubernetes, Helm, GitOps

Ship with the Helm chart and operator; scrape Prometheus; drive from Argo CD / GitOps. Clients: CLI plus Go, Python, Rust, TypeScript SDKs, and an MCP server for agent tooling. Getting started: GETTING-STARTED.md.

9. Guided tours (videos and site)

Tour Where What you see

Features#featuresEngines behind one API
Architecture#architectureActive/active region mesh + CLI demo
Security model#securityAudit, Shamir, tenant isolation, no plaintext
Full presentationyoutu.be/O6q3_H0k2M8~20 min deep walkthrough

Presentation chapters (YouTube)

1:30What WSLVault is

content.title: Workstation AI Shop on Ring Promoter: Orbit, Version-Verified Health and the Path from INT to PROD
content.sub_title: Technical guide: shop Helm/CI mapping, Orbit semantics, version-verified health for the AI agent, secrets per ring, promote API, and a production checklist
content.content:
This article is the release-engineering deep dive for Workstation AI Shop — the storefront at shop.workstation.co.uk that sells GPU machines and uses a fully autonomous AI Sales Agent to configure baskets. Companion blog (stakeholder-friendly): Promoting the AI Shop through the rings. Control-plane reference: ringpromoter.com.

Watch on YouTube · Product: ringpromoter.com

1. System under promotion

Workstation AI Shop is a Next.js server app (Helm chart shop-chart) on k3s. The browser talks only to the shop; the shop BFF calls OpsAPI in-cluster (http://workstation-opsapi/). Payments use Stripe Checkout with webhooks on OpsAPI. Catalogue freshness is a CronJob (market/sync.mjs). The AI Sales Agent uses Anthropic (ANTHROPIC_MODEL, typically claude-sonnet-5-5, CHAT_MAX_TURNS capped) — if the key is missing, chat shows offline and the rest of the shop still works.

Public hosts

  • INT: https://int-shop.workstation.co.uk
  • PROD: https://shop.workstation.co.uk

Edge path (prod): Cloudflare DNS (DNS-only) → wslproxy → Traefik on the edge node → shop Ingress. Prod has been pinned to a dedicated edge worker where required for latency and certificate locality.

2. Why Ring Promoter owns the hop, not the build

CI still builds and pushes wsw-shop:<sha7>. Ring Promoter answers a different question: is this exact version healthy in ring N, and is it allowed into ring N+1 right now? That matches the product framing on ringpromoter.com:

  1. One ring at a time — promote always targets the next ring.
  2. Source must prove health before anything deploys.
  3. Target must earn health after deploy (retries, then auto-rollback).
  4. Failure undoes itself to the previous recorded version.
  5. Every seed / promote / rollback is written to history.

Shop-specific risk amplifies those rules: the AI agent, market sync and BFF trust keys must move together. A “green Helm job” that leaves an old chat binary answering is a silent sales failure.

3. Reading the Orbit screenshot (release semantics)

From the console capture used in this article:

  • Application name: Workstation AI Shop (human label on the roster and Orbit node).
  • Version in flight: 7cd70f6 (short git SHA — matches image tag convention).
  • Current ring: INT — status Deploying; copy such as “has reached int, N rings to go.”
  • Pipeline legend: int → test → acc → prod across the top of Orbit.
  • Signals: blue node = deployment in progress; green trail = how far the newest version earned; Earth = PROD / live users.
  • SLO breadcrumbs: TTFB ~71ms, location London, GB — useful in the same pane as promotion state so latency regressions are not a separate tool hop.

Lanes (APP × INT/TEST/ACC/PROD matrix) is the complementary view when you need to see whether PROD lags the SHA that already spans ACC.

4. Mapping rings to shop deploy mechanics

Ring Shop mechanism Gate intent
INTGitHub Actions shop-deploy.yaml on main paths under shop/** / chart → deploys intEngineer smoke: /api/health, agent turns, catalogue read
TESTRing Promoter promote INT→TEST (same image SHA)Automated regression; market sync dry observations
ACCPromote TEST→ACCStakeholder UX on AI basket; quote PDF; optional Stripe test mode
PRODPromote ACC→PROD (+ production password). Chart prod may also be workflow_dispatch with TARGET_ENV=prod — Ring Promoter should remain the ledger of what customers runHuman gate; live secrets from vault path workstation-shop/prod/config

Important: treat Helm/workflow deploy as the deployer implementation detail. Ring Promoter remains the system of record for which SHA is current / previous per ring and whether the hop was rolled back.

5. Version-verified health for an AI storefront

Configure the shop health endpoint (or a dedicated readiness field) so Ring Promoter can assert the deployed SHA — via health_version_field or health_version_header as documented on the product site. That catches:

  • Old ReplicaSets still answering while the new Deployment is stuck.
  • Edge/cache serving a previous HTML shell in front of a mixed API.
  • Agent worker and web process skew (chat binary ≠ storefront SHA).

Also verify the source ring reports the same version before promote — so you never promote a SHA that INT already lost.

6. Secrets and AI agent continuity across rings

Per devops/SHOP-DEPLOY.md:

  • Vault: workstation-shop/<env>/config → ESO → shop-secret-<ns>.
  • CI runtime Secret shop-runtime-<ns> may supply ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPSAPI_ADMIN_API_KEY, FIRECRAWL_API_KEY.
  • SHOP_BFF_KEY must match OpsAPI’s key for that env or the BFF is treated as anonymous.
  • Prod uses an isolated vault token / SecretStore so rotating INT cannot touch PROD.

Promotion does not invent secrets — but a ring that is “healthy” while the agent is offline is a business-visible defect. Include agent liveness in the health definition you gate on.

7. CI integration shape

After the image is published and INT is seeded (or after the int workflow lands the SHA), promotion is fail-closed HTTP:

curl --fail -sS -X POST "$RP/api/apps/$APP/seed" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"ring\":\"int\",\"version\":\"$VERSION\"}"

curl --fail -sS -X POST "$RP/api/apps/$APP/promote" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"from_ring":"int"}'

Non-2xx fails the job. 422 means the operation ran, failed health, and rolled back — evidence is in Ring Promoter history / job steps, not only in GitHub Actions logs. Optional ?async=1 returns a job id for live step polling (lock → source health → deploy → target health → record).

8. Auto-promote policy we recommend for the shop

  • ON for early rings when smoke + version health are strong (e.g. INT→TEST).
  • HOLD on ACC so product can sign off AI basket behaviour.
  • Never config-enable auto-promote into PROD — require production password / human promote.
  • Rollbacks remain exempt from the prod password so incidents are not blocked.

Optional gates (maintenance windows, version-specific Go/No-Go, Jira CR, Grafana panels with max_age) run before deploy so a failed gate leaves every ring untouched.

9. Failure modes this design prevents

Failure Without Ring Promoter With protocol
Skipped stagingHotfix workflow_dispatch to prodCannot skip rings by design
Green job, old chatHTTP 200 from previous ReplicaSetVersion-verified health → rollback
Half-updated prodCI timeout aborts mid-rolloutDetached op context + advisory lock
Secret skew INT vs PRODShared token blast radiusIsolated prod SecretStore + ring-scoped config
Unclear “what’s live?”Slack archaeologyOrbit/Lanes + per-ring history

10. Operational checklist (shop release)

  1. Confirm image wsw-shop:<sha7> published.
  2. INT host healthy; agent completes a basket configuration turn; /api/health reports SHA.
  3. Promote through TEST → ACC; re-run market sync observation if catalogue code changed.
  4. Stakeholder sign-off on ACC (AI copy, quote terms, checkout/quote path).
  5. Promote to PROD with production password; verify shop.workstation.co.uk SHA + TTFB.
  6. Leave Orbit open during soak — blue should clear to healthy green on PROD.

11. Related reading

  • Ring Promoter product · Compare vs Argo CD / Kargo / CI
  • Every release earns production · Protocol deep dive
  • QA gates before production
  • Which tool answers which release question
  • In-repo runbook: devops/SHOP-DEPLOY.md

content.title: Ring Promoter vs Argo CD, Kargo, Spinnaker and CI: Release Workflow Design and Architecture Decision Records
content.sub_title: Technical deep dive: full feature matrix, head-to-heads, three release workflow designs, failure modes prevented, and worked ADRs with a decision checklist
content.content:
Release tooling is usually chosen by feature list and then lived with for years. This article takes a different route. It starts from the question each tool is built to answer, compares Ring Promoter with Argo CD, Flux, Kargo, Spinnaker, Octopus Deploy, Harness and CI pipelines using Ring Promoter’s own comparison at ringpromoter.com/compare, designs three release workflows around the result, and then shows how to capture the decision in Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) so it can be audited, explained and revisited.

Companion reading: the short version of this piece is the blog post Which Tool Answers Which Release Question. The promotion protocol itself is covered in Every Release Earns Production, and gate placement in QA Gates Before Production.

About the sources. Statements about Ring Promoter come from its README and from ringpromoter.com. Statements about other products summarise Ring Promoter’s own comparison page; they are a vendor’s view of its competitors. Products change, so verify each row against the vendor’s current documentation before it informs a decision.

1. Start with the question, not the feature list

The compare page frames the market around three questions:

Tool familyQuestion it answersWhat it leaves to you
Argo CD / Flux“Does the cluster match the manifests in Git?”Moving a version from staging to production: a PR, an image updater, or another tool such as Kargo.
CI pipelines (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab)“Did the deploy job exit 0?”A record of what runs in each environment, and automatic rollback. A green job can leave the old version answering 200 OK.
Ring Promoter“Is this exact version healthy here, and is it allowed into the next ring right now?”Git sync and drift detection, and traffic shifting inside a ring.

Ring Promoter’s model, from its README, is an ordered set of shared rings, int (Integration) → test (Test) → acc (Acceptance) → prod (Production), with current and previous version and full history kept per (application, ring). Promotion moves one ring at a time and never skips. The source ring must be healthy before a promotion starts; after deploying, the target is health-checked with a configurable number of retries; if it is still unhealthy it is rolled back automatically to its previous version; and every seed, promote, rollback and restart is written to history, success or failure.

2. The feature matrix

The table below reproduces the compare page’s matrix. “Yes” means built in; “Partial” means it needs an add-on, plugin, paid tier or custom script; “No” means not provided. Notes in brackets are the compare page’s own qualifiers.

Capability Ring Promoter Argo CD Flux Kargo Spinnaker Octopus Harness GH Actions envs
Promotion model
Ordered environment promotionYes (never skip; current, previous, history per app and ring)No (promote by PR)NoYes (Stages + Freight)Yes (pipeline stages)Yes (Lifecycles)YesPartial (no ledger)
Kubernetes and VM apps in one control planeYes (kubectl, K8s Jobs, GitHub Actions dispatch)No (Kubernetes only)No (Kubernetes only)No (Kubernetes only)YesYesYesYes
Opt-in auto-promote per ring, hard stop before prodYes (config cannot enable auto-promote into prod)NoNoYesYesYesYesPartial
Verification and rollback
Version-verified health checkYes (JSON field or header; also checks source ring)No (resource health only)NoPartial (custom AnalysisTemplate)Partial (custom stage)Partial (script step)Partial (custom verify)No
Automatic rollback on failed healthYes (runs detached)Partial (needs Argo Rollouts)Partial (needs Flagger)Partial (via Rollouts)YesPartial (scripted)YesNo
Rejects a non-existent version before deployingYes (400 before any dispatch)NoNoYes (Freight from warehouse)PartialYes (packages)YesNo
Release governance (checked before any deploy)
Maintenance windowsYes (opened inline from promote dialog)Yes (sync windows)NoPartial (via Argo CD)Yes (execution windows)Yes (deployment freezes)Yes (freeze windows)No (wait timer only)
Go/No-Go sign-off for an exact versionYes (with QA status and engineer)No (Git PR review)NoYes (manual promotion)Yes (manual judgment)YesYesYes (required reviewers)
Jira change-request validationYesNoNoNoPartial (plugin)Partial (paid tier)YesPartial (third-party action)
Dashboard metrics as a release gateYes (Grafana; max_age stale detection)NoPartial (Flagger)Yes (Analysis)Yes (Kayenta)PartialYesNo
Where Ring Promoter is not the better choice
Git as source of truth, drift detection, self-healNo (its database is the source of truth)YesYesYesNoPartialYesNo
Canary / blue-green traffic shiftingNo (whole-ring deploys)Partial (Argo Rollouts)Partial (Flagger)PartialYesPartialYesNo
SSO and fine-grained RBACNo (API bearer token + prod password)YesPartial (K8s RBAC)YesYesYesYesYes
Operational footprintSmall (one Go binary; Postgres or in-memory)MediumMediumLarge (Argo CD + Rollouts + Kargo)Large (about 10 services)Medium (server + SQL, or SaaS)Large (SaaS or heavy self-host)Small (hosted)

Two things stand out. First, the last block is unusual for a vendor page: it lists four rows where Ring Promoter loses. Second, the rows where it wins cluster around one idea, which is verifying that a specific version is running and allowed before the next step. That is the gap between “the deploy finished” and “this release has earned production”.

3. Head to head

Argo CD

According to the compare page, Argo CD is better at keeping clusters in sync with Git and fixing drift, at multi-cluster scale with SSO and project RBAC, and it has a large CNCF community. Ring Promoter is better at moving a version from int to prod (“Argo CD has no promotion model”), checking the running version and rolling back automatically, change windows, sign-offs, Jira CRs and Grafana gates, and apps that do not run on Kubernetes. The verdict: Argo CD is a sync engine; Ring Promoter is a release control plane. An Argo CD deployer is on Ring Promoter’s V2 roadmap so the two can run together.

Kargo

Kargo is the closest match: promotion on top of Argo CD. It is better at GitOps-native promotion (it writes to Git) and traffic-level analysis through Argo Rollouts. Ring Promoter needs no Argo CD, Rollouts or CRDs (“one binary instead of three systems”), handles VM and CI-driven apps alongside Kubernetes, has built-in maintenance windows, Jira CR and Grafana gates, and offers version-verified health without writing AnalysisTemplates. The verdict: fully committed to Argo CD on Kubernetes, look at Kargo; mixed estate or no GitOps stack yet, Ring Promoter has less to run.

Spinnaker

Spinnaker is better at multi-cloud (AWS, GCP, Azure) deployment strategies and canary analysis with Kayenta. Ring Promoter is one Go binary rather than about ten Java services, apps are added with config only, and version-verified health and Jira CR gates are built in. The verdict: Spinnaker suits large platform teams who can staff it.

Octopus Deploy and Harness

These commercial platforms are better at breadth (many deploy targets, templates and integrations) and at enterprise access control, audit and vendor support. Ring Promoter has no per-seat or per-service licence, is self-hosted with data and AI diagnosis on your own infrastructure, is small enough to read the whole promotion engine, and keeps your existing GitHub Actions workflows instead of replacing them. The compare page calls Octopus lifecycles and Harness pipelines the closest in concept.

GitHub Actions, GitLab CI and Jenkins

CI is better at building, testing, packaging and anything you can script. Ring Promoter is better at knowing what runs in every ring now and what ran before, rolling back automatically when health fails, and stopping a prod deploy outside a change window. The verdict is the one to remember: “Not a replacement. CI produces the version; Ring Promoter moves it. Your deploy workflow becomes one of Ring Promoter’s deployers.”

4. Release workflow designs

The comparison only becomes useful when it shapes a workflow. Below are three designs built from documented Ring Promoter behaviour. Config and commands are taken from the project README and its sample config.yaml; app names are the README’s examples.

Design A: CI seed, automatic early rings, gated production

This is the pattern the README describes as typical. CI builds and pushes an image, seeds int, and optionally promotes once:

RP=https://ring-promoter.example.com
APP=web-frontend
TOKEN=${RING_PROMOTER_TOKEN}   # from CI secrets
VERSION=$GITHUB_SHA            # the image tag you just pushed

curl --fail -sS -X POST "$RP/api/apps/$APP/seed" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"ring\":\"int\",\"version\":\"$VERSION\"}"

curl --fail -sS -X POST "$RP/api/apps/$APP/promote" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"from_ring":"int"}'

Calls run synchronously by default and return 200 on success or 422 when the operation ran but failed (for example, the health check failed and the target was rolled back), so curl --fail turns a failed promotion into a failed CI step. Add ?async=1 to get 202 with a job ID and poll GET /api/apps/{app}/jobs/{id} instead.

Auto-promote then carries the version onward. Declaring it in config makes config the owner of the switch:

rings:
  int:  { namespace: int,  ... }                     # unset: operator-controlled
  test: { namespace: test, ..., auto_promote: true }  # config-owned: on
  acc:  { namespace: acc,  ..., auto_promote: false } # config-owned: off

With test on, a version that lands healthy in test continues to acc inside the same operation and lock. With acc off, nothing reaches prod without a human. The README is precise about the three states: absent keeps the runtime API toggle; an explicit value is applied at every start-up, and the API toggle returns 409 for that ring. Config may not set auto_promote: true on the ring before production, which is refused at start-up so config cannot bypass the production password.

Gates guard the sensitive rings. From the sample config.yaml:

promotion_policy:
  maintenance_window:
    rings: [prod]
    recurring:
      - days: [Sat, Sun]      # empty = every day
        start: "02:00"        # HH:MM, in `timezone`
        end:   "04:00"        # end < start crosses midnight
        timezone: Europe/London   # empty = UTC
  qa_signoff:
    rings: [acc, prod]
  change_request:
    rings: [acc, prod]
    provider: jira            # test | jira
    jira:
      base_url: https://your-org.atlassian.net
      email: releases@your-org.com
      token_env: RP_JIRA_TOKEN        # default
      allowed_statuses: [Approved, "Ready for Release"]   # empty = any issue
      project_keys: [CR, OPS]         # optional prefix guard

A Grafana gate can be added for slow signals such as nightly end-to-end suites, with go_min, no_go_max, a list of checks and max_age. Two interactions matter for workflow design. Auto-promote into a change-request-gated ring fails closed, because there is no interactive CR code, so such rings are always promoted into explicitly. And auto-promote into a Grafana-gated ring stops at a no-go, because an override needs a human reason. The final hop needs the production password (RP_PROD_PASSWORD) in the request body; rollbacks are exempt.

Two operational details from the README are easy to miss. The CI example deliberately seeds only into the first ring; higher rings are “typically promoted deliberately from the UI or a separate approved job using the same promote call”. And the demo CR code test is always accepted whatever the provider, which is convenient for demos and worth stating in your ADR so nobody mistakes it for a production control.

Design B: a mixed Kubernetes and VM estate

Many estates are not all Kubernetes. Ring Promoter selects the deployer per application, so one control plane can promote both. Kubernetes apps use KubectlDeployer (kubectl set image plus rollout status) or the k8sjob deployer, which runs each operation as a Kubernetes Job with the runner contract RP_APP, RP_RING, RP_VERSION, RP_TARGET_ENV and RP_EXECUTION_ID. VM apps with an existing pipeline use GitHubActionsDeployer, which dispatches the workflow, waits for the run and applies the same health check and rollback.

The README’s real example is wslproxy, an OpenResty/Lua app on VMs:

apps:
  - name: wslproxy
    deployer: github                      # override the global deployer
    github:
      owner: bwalia
      repo: wslproxy
      workflow: deploy-single-environment.yml   # per-env deploy, no cascade
      ref: main                           # branch hosting the workflow (default)
      deploy_mode: full                   # value sent as the DEPLOY_MODE input
      token_env: RP_GITHUB_TOKEN          # env holding the API token (Secret)
      poll_interval: 20s                  # how often the run is polled
      run_lookup_timeout: 90s             # wait for the dispatched run to appear

The design lesson is in the README’s warning: point the deployer at a workflow that deploys exactly one environment. A cumulative delivery pipeline, where each stage depends on the previous one, would turn a single-ring deploy into a run all the way to production, and a prod rollback could revert lower rings. For GitHub-deployed apps, seed also checks that the branch, tag or SHA exists and rejects a typo with 400 before dispatching anything.

Design C: pairing with Argo CD, Argo Rollouts or Flagger

The compare page recommends pairing rather than replacing: “Argo CD or Flux, with Ring Promoter for promotion” where Git must be the source of truth for cluster state, and “Argo Rollouts or Flagger, alongside either” for percentage-based canary traffic. Today there is no Argo CD deployer (it is planned for V2), so a pairing needs a deliberate design. These are our design notes, not built-in features:

  • Decide who owns the image tag. If Argo CD self-heals a Deployment and Ring Promoter’s KubectlDeployer runs kubectl set image on the same object, the two tools may disagree about the desired state. Give each field one owner. One option is the k8sjob deployer, whose runner script receives RP_VERSION and RP_TARGET_ENV and could update the environment’s Git configuration for Argo CD to sync; the exit code decides success.
  • Let version-verified health close the loop. With health_version_field or health_version_header set, Ring Promoter only reports success when the endpoint reports the version just deployed, however the change reached the cluster. Size retry.count, retry.delay and operation_timeout to cover the time sync and rollout take.
  • Treat canary as inside a ring. Ring Promoter deploys a ring as a whole. Argo Rollouts or Flagger can shift traffic within that ring; Ring Promoter then decides whether the version may enter the next ring. During a canary, a health endpoint may be served by either version, so check how your health URL routes before enabling version verification there.

Whatever you choose, record it. This is exactly the kind of cross-tool contract that is obvious to the person who designed it and opaque to everyone else.

5. Failure modes this setup prevents

The value of a promotion control plane shows up in the failures it removes. Each of these is documented behaviour.

Failure modeWhat happens without a controlRing Promoter mechanism
Green deploy, old codeThe deploy job succeeds but old pods still answer 200 OK; the release is marked done.Version-verified health: the endpoint must report the exact version just deployed, otherwise the check fails and the ring rolls back. The source ring is verified too.
Aborted rollbackA CI runner timeout or load-balancer idle timeout kills the request mid-deploy, leaving a ring half-changed.Operations run on a context detached from the HTTP request, bounded by operation_timeout, so neither the deploy nor its rollback can be cut off.
Stale metrics read as GOA nightly suite quietly stops running and its last green result shows forever.max_age turns an old result into NO DATA. An unreachable Grafana is advisory, so an observability outage does not become a release outage, and the UI never shows it as a GO.
Half-finished releaseA gate fails after some rings have changed.Gates are checked before any deploy; a failed gate leaves all state untouched.
Concurrent promotionsAn accidental scale-up runs two promotions on the same app.A Postgres session advisory lock serialises operations per app across replicas.
Skipped environmentA version jumps from test straight to prod.promote {from_ring} always targets the next ring; rings are never skipped.
Typo’d versionA non-existent ref triggers a doomed workflow run.For GitHub-deployed apps, seed rejects it with 400 before dispatch.
Sign-off reused for a different buildApproval for v1 is treated as approval for v2.Go/No-Go sign-offs are version-specific: a GO for v1 does not authorise v2.

6. Architecture Decision Records

The previous sections contain at least five decisions with long-lived consequences: which tool owns promotion, which owns sync, whether version verification is mandatory, which rings auto-promote, and how the limits are mitigated. Decisions like these tend to live in a chat thread or one engineer’s head. Architecture Decision Records give them a durable home.

What an ADR is

An ADR is a short document that records one significant decision, the context that forced it, and its consequences. The format most teams start from was proposed by Michael Nygard in 2011 in “Documenting Architecture Decisions”. It has five parts:

  1. Title: a short noun phrase, numbered (for example “ADR-001: Use Ring Promoter for environment promotion”).
  2. Status: proposed, accepted, deprecated or superseded (with a link to the replacing ADR).
  3. Context: the forces at play, technical, organisational and regulatory, stated neutrally.
  4. Decision: what we will do, in active voice (“We will…”).
  5. Consequences: what becomes easier and what becomes harder, including the costs.

MADR (Markdown Any Decision Records) is a popular alternative with more structure: a problem statement, decision drivers, considered options, the decision outcome and the pros and cons of each option. It suits decisions like this one, where the considered options (Argo CD alone, Kargo, Ring Promoter, a commercial platform) are themselves useful to record. Either format works; consistency within a repository matters more than the choice.

Why ADRs matter for release tooling

  • Reversibility. Release tooling sits on the path to production. Swapping it later touches every pipeline and every on-call runbook. An ADR forces the team to write down what would make the decision wrong before it is expensive to change.
  • Audit. When a change-management reviewer asks why prod promotions require a CR code and a password but rollbacks do not, the ADR is the answer, with the date and the people who accepted it. Ring Promoter’s history table records what happened; the ADR records why the controls exist.
  • Onboarding. A new engineer who finds Argo CD installed but not deciding promotions will reasonably assume a mistake. One page of context prevents a well-meant “fix”.
  • Revisiting when constraints change. The compare page lists limits that may not last: no SSO or per-user RBAC yet, no Argo CD deployer until V2. Writing “revisit when SSO lands” into the consequences turns a known gap into a trigger.

Lifecycle and storage

An ADR is born proposed, usually as a pull request. Review happens in the PR, where the people affected can comment. Merging marks it accepted. When circumstances change, you do not rewrite the accepted ADR; you write a new one that supersedes it, and update the old one’s status to point forward. Some ADRs are rejected, and keeping those is valuable too, because they stop the same debate recurring.

Store ADRs in the repository they govern, typically docs/adr/ with numbered file names such as 0001-use-ring-promoter-for-promotion.md. Keeping them beside the config means a change to promotion_policy and the ADR that justifies it can be reviewed together. Tools such as Nat Pryce’s adr-tools automate numbering and linking, but a directory and a template are enough to start.

A note on sources: the Ring Promoter repository contains design documents (for example docs/kubernetes-executor-design.md) but no ADR directory at the time of writing, so the records below are worked examples for your own repository, not summaries of the project’s internal decisions.

Worked example: ADR-001

# ADR-001: Use Ring Promoter for environment promotion; keep Argo CD for cluster sync

Status: Accepted, 2026-10-05
Deciders: platform team, release management, SRE lead

## Context
- Our estate mixes Kubernetes services and VM services (OpenResty) that are
  deployed by existing GitHub Actions workflows.
- Argo CD already keeps our clusters in sync with Git. It has no promotion
  model: moving a version from acc to prod is a manual PR today.
- Change management requires a maintenance window, a QA Go/No-Go for the exact
  version and an approved Jira change request before production changes.
- Options considered: Argo CD + PRs (status quo), Kargo, Ring Promoter,
  a commercial release platform.
- Kargo requires Argo CD and Kubernetes; it would not cover our VM services.

## Decision
We will use Ring Promoter to promote versions int -> test -> acc -> prod for
all services. Kubernetes services use the kubectl or k8sjob deployer; VM
services use the github deployer pointed at single-environment workflows.
Argo CD continues to own cluster sync for platform components it manages
today. No Deployment will have its image tag owned by both tools.

## Consequences
Positive
- One record of current, previous and historical versions per app and ring.
- Automatic rollback on failed health; gates checked before any deploy.
- VM services keep their workflows; no rewrite.
Negative
- No SSO or per-user RBAC in Ring Promoter. Mitigation: access only through
  our authenticating reverse proxy; API token held in CI secrets only.
- Ring state lives in Postgres, not Git. Postgres becomes part of the release
  path and is backed up accordingly. No drift detection from this tool.
- Smaller ecosystem: deployers are kubectl, Kubernetes Jobs and GitHub Actions.
Revisit when
- Ring Promoter ships SSO/RBAC, or an Argo CD deployer (listed for V2).
- More than half our services move to a GitOps-only model.

Worked example: ADR-002

# ADR-002: Require version-verified health checks on every ring

Status: Accepted, 2026-10-05
Relates to: ADR-001

## Context
- A plain URL health check can pass while the previous version still serves
  traffic: a deploy job can succeed while old pods still answer 200 OK.
- Ring Promoter supports health_version_field (a JSON field, dotted paths
  allowed) or health_version_header on a ring. When set, every post-deploy
  check must report the exact version just deployed, and the source ring is
  verified before promotion.

## Decision
Every service will expose its deployed version (image tag or ref) on its
health endpoint, and every ring will set health_version_field or
health_version_header. New services are not onboarded without it.

## Consequences
Positive
- "Green deploy, old code" fails the check and triggers automatic rollback.
- Promotions only start from a source ring proven to run that version.
Negative
- Each service needs a small code change to report its version.
- Rings that pin a ref (ref: release) record the version the endpoint reports
  instead of verifying a known one; we accept this for release-branch apps.
- During any in-ring canary, the endpoint may be served by either version;
  such rings need their health URL reviewed before enabling verification.

Worked example: ADR-003

# ADR-003: Human gate before production; auto-promote only early rings

Status: Accepted, 2026-10-05
Relates to: ADR-001, ADR-002

## Context
- Auto-promote can chain hops inside one operation and lock, stopping at the
  first ring with the flag off or on any failure.
- Ring Promoter refuses auto_promote: true in config on the ring before prod;
  enabling it via the API requires the production password.
- Auto-promote into a change-request-gated ring fails closed, and into a
  Grafana-gated ring stops at a no-go.

## Decision
- test declares auto_promote: true; acc declares auto_promote: false.
  Both are config-owned so the state is visible in Git and reviewed.
- acc and prod require qa_signoff and a Jira change_request; prod also
  requires an open maintenance window and RP_PROD_PASSWORD.
- Grafana overrides are allowed only with a written override_reason, and
  are reviewed weekly from the job log.

## Consequences
Positive
- Fast feedback through int, test and acc with no clicks.
- Nothing reaches production without a named human, an exact-version GO
  and an approved CR.
Negative
- Production releases wait for a window and a person; we accept the latency.
- Rollbacks are exempt from the password by design; incident response is
  never blocked, so access to the rollback API must itself be controlled.
- The demo CR code "test" is always accepted; we must never rely on CR
  validation alone as a security control.

Decision checklist

Before accepting an ADR in this space, check each item:

  • Which question are we answering: sync (“does the cluster match Git?”), build (“did the job pass?”) or promotion (“is this version healthy and allowed next?”)?
  • Is any part of our estate outside Kubernetes? If so, which tools in the shortlist can deploy to it?
  • Must Git be the only source of truth for cluster state? If so, how will promotion state and Git stay consistent?
  • Do we need traffic shifting inside an environment, and which tool provides it?
  • Do we need SSO and per-user RBAC now? If the chosen tool lacks it, what is the interim control?
  • Can every service report its deployed version on its health endpoint?
  • Which rings may auto-promote, and is the hop into production always deliberate?
  • Which gates apply to which rings: maintenance window, version-specific sign-off, change request, metrics?
  • What does a rollback require, and who can trigger it?
  • What is the operational footprint we are willing to run, and who staffs it?
  • Have competitor claims been checked against current vendor documentation?
  • What specific events will make us revisit this decision?

7. Summary

Argo CD and Flux keep clusters in line with Git. CI produces a version. Ring Promoter, by its own description, decides what earns production: it moves one exact version through int, test, acc and prod, checks each ring is really running it, enforces change windows, sign-offs, Jira CRs and Grafana gates before anything changes, and rolls back by itself when health fails, for Kubernetes and VM apps from one binary. It does not do GitOps, traffic shifting or SSO today, and its ecosystem is smaller. Those trade-offs are acceptable for some teams and not for others. The way to make the call well is to answer the checklist honestly and write the outcome down in an ADR that says when to look again.

Further reading: ringpromoter.com/compare, ringpromoter.com, the TenthMatrix Ring Promoter page, Ring Promoter: Modern CI/CD for AI-Powered Deployments and Ring Promoter v1.0.2: Rings, Orbit and Lanes.

content.title: GitLab Runners على Kubernetes: تحسين التكاليف على نطاق واسع باستخدام مشغل Kubernetes
content.sub_title: المشغل مقابل Helm، قيم تنفيذ Kubernetes، التوازي، دين-دي-إن، أذرع التوسع التلقائي، المراقبة وقائمة التحقق من FinOps
content.content:
غوص تقني عميق: GitLab Runners على Kubernetes، تثبيت المشغل، قيم Helm، التوسع التلقائي ونموذج FinOps للتكاليف. للحصول على الإصدار المختصر، اقرأتوقف عن دفع ثمن CI غير النشط.

الخلاصة.خصّص للذروة، وألغِ الخصخصة في القاع. حاويات المهام المؤقتة تستعيد CPU والذاكرة والتخزين عند انخفاض الطلب — خاصةً في الليالي والأيام العطلية.

معظم الفرق تدفع ثمن التكامل المستمر وكأن كل ليلة وكل عطلة لا تزال صباح الاثنين. الخوادم تظل ساخنة. القرص يبقى مخصصًا. لا أحد يدمج أكوادًا — والفاتورة لا تلاحظ ذلك. هذه الجملة ليست شعارًا؛ إنها الشكل الافتراضي لأسطول مشغّلات ثابت.

هذا المقال الطويل هو المرافق التقني لرحلة عملية لـGitLab Server وGitLab Runner على Kubernetes: كيف يحول مشغّل Kubernetes كل مهمة CI إلى حاوية مؤقتة، وكيف يمكّن ذلك من تخصيص وإلغاء تخصيص السعة ديناميكيًا، وكيف يفتح هذا التصميم بابًا لـتوفير هائل في التكاليفباستعادة CPU والذاكرة والتخزين عندما ينهار الطلب بين عشية وضحاها وفي عطلة نهاية الأسبوع.

شاهد كلا الجلسات أولًا، ثم استخدم هذه الصفحة كنموذج معماري وتكاليف مكتوب.

1. المشغّلات والأنابيب— توسيع أحمال GitLab Runner تلقائيًا باستخدام Kubernetes.

شاهد: GitLab Runners وCI/CD على Kubernetes بشكل كامل· الإصدار المبسط:توقف عن دفع ثمن CI غير النشط

2. خادم GitLab على HA Kubernetes— قم بتنفيذ GitLab باستخدام المشغل خلال دقائق قليلة.

شاهد: قم بتنفيذ GitLab في مجموعة HA Kubernetes باستخدام المشغل· الوثائق:تثبيت مشغل GitLab

1. الأطروحة

GitLab على Kubernetes + مشغل Kubernetesيغير وحدة سعة CI من "آلة نمتلكها طوال الشهر" إلى "حاويات (و عُقَد) نؤجرها للعمل". يبقى مدير التشغيل المستمر صغيرًا ودائمًا نشطًا. تظهر حاويات التشغيل المستمر لبناء معين ثم تختفي بعد ذلك. مع التوسع التلقائي للمجموعة، تتبع عُقَد العمال نفس المنحنى. هكذا تحمي الإنتاجية في صباح يوم الاثنين وتتوقف عن دفع أسعار صباح يوم الاثنين ليوم الثلاثاء الساعة 03:00 ولأيام السبت الهادئة.

في سطر واحد — نفس السطر في الدليل المبسط:قم بتوفير الموارد لذروة الحمل، وقم بإلغاء توفيرها لحدود الحمل.

2. عادة التكلفة العالية، التي تُصنف كعيب معماري

CI التقليدي غالبًا ما يبدو كأسطول دائم: مجموعة ثابتة من آلات البناء التي تبقى «للتأمين». هذا النهج يعمل عندما يكون الزخم مستقرًا. لكنه يهدر المال عندما يكون الطلب متقطعًا.

  • نهارًا:المطورون يفرغون الفروع، يفتحون طلبات الدمج، ويشغّلون الاختبارات — يزداد الطلب.
  • المساء والليل:ينخفض النشاط؛ والآلات لا تزال تستهلك CPU والذاكرة العشوائية.
  • عطلة نهاية الأسبوع:غالبًا شبه خامل — ومع ذلك قد لا تزال أحجام التخزين والعُقد السحابية محجوزة ومُفوترة.

لا تدفع مقابل «البناء المنجز». بل تدفع مقابل السعة الموجودة سواء استخدمها أحد أم لا. الأساطيل الثابتة تتراكم فيها أيضًا حالة ملتصقة: «يعمل على المشغّل 3»، حزم انحرفت، ذاكرة مخزنة لا تنتهي صلاحيتها. القوالب المرنة وحدها لا تحل الانضباط، لكنها تجعل البدء من الصفر هو الافتراضي.

3. خريطة النظام

الطبقةالدورالموقع النموذجي
خادم GitLabإدارة SCM، تنسيق CI، السجل، واجهة المستخدم/APIKubernetes عبر GitLab Operator / مخطط Helm (مثل k3s lab)
مدير Runnerوكيل مسجل يقوم بجلب المهامإصدار Helm في مساحة اسم مخصصة (مثلgitlab-runner)

4. تثبيت GitLab على المجموعة (مسار المشغل)

مسار التدريب في اليوم الأول يقوم بتثبيت GitLab باستخدام المشغل الرسمي، بحيث يشارك الخادم نفس Kubernetes الأساس الذي تستخدمه الوحدات الفرعية. يشرح الفيديو المرافقنشر GitLab في مجموعة Kubernetes عالية التوفر باستخدام المشغلعملية التثبيت خلال دقائق معدودة. المتطلبات المسبقة: مجموعة مزودة بـ ingress و Helm وkubectlو cert-manager عندما يدير الرسم البياني TLS.

helm repo add gitlab https://charts.gitlab.io
helm repo update

helm install gitlab-operator gitlab/gitlab-operator \
  --create-namespace \
  --namespace gitlab-system

kubectl -n gitlab-system get deployment gitlab-controller-manager

# Apply the GitLab custom resource (pin chart version in the manifest)
kubectl -n gitlab-system apply -f deploy_gitlab_server.yaml

نموذج CR (يمكنك تخصيص النطاق و البريد الإلكتروني للمصدر ليناسب بيئتك):

apiVersion: apps.gitlab.com/v1beta1
kind: GitLab
metadata:
  name: gitlab
spec:
  chart:
    version: "9.2.2"
    values:
      global:
        hosts:
          domain: "example.com"
        ingress:
          configureCertmanager: true
      certmanager-issuer:
        email: you@example.com

يستغرق التثبيت الأولي عادةً ما بين 10 إلى 15 دقيقة بينما تستقر مكونات الخدمة الجانبية و Sidekiq وقواعد البيانات والمكونات ذات الصلة. احصل على كلمة المرور الجذرية الأولية من السري في المجموعة:

kubectl get secret gitlab-gitlab-initial-root-password -n gitlab-system \
  -o jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 -d

المرجع:تثبيت مشغل GitLab(تبويب Helm على تلك الصفحة). نظرة عامة على الرسم البياني:docs.gitlab.com/charts· دليل التثبيت:تثبيت الرسم البياني.

5. GitLab Runner مع Kubernetes كمُنفِّذ

GitLab Runner هو التطبيق الذي يعمل مع GitLab CI/CD لتشغيل المهام في خط الأنابيب. معKubernetes كمُنفِّذ، لا يقوم المدير بالتجميع على نفسه. بالنسبة لكل مهمة يقوم بـ:

  1. إنشاء حاوية (بالإضافة إلى حاويات المساعدة/الخدمة حسب الإعداد).
  2. إرسال السجلات مرة أخرى إلى GitLab.
  3. جمع المنتجات النهائية وحالة الخروج.
  4. حذف الحاوية — مما يعيد CPU والذاكرة إلى المجموعة.

يمثل حلقة الإنشاء/التشغيل/الحذف أول رافعة للتكلفة. يجب ألا تترك الأعمال المنجزة آلة دافئة مخصصة طوال الليل.

نمط التثبيت 5.1 لـ Helm

تُنشئ سكريبتات التدريب مساحة أسماء، وتُمرر رمز تسجيل، وقد تقوم بتثبيت أكثر من إصدار (على سبيل المثال، مشغّلات تعتمد على Alpine وأخرى تعتمد على Ubuntu) حتى يتمكن الوظائف من اختيار بيئات مختلفة. الإجراء الرسمي:قم بتثبيت GitLab Runner باستخدام الرسم البياني Helm; مرجع القيم:قم بتكوين رسم بياني GitLab Runner Helm.

helm upgrade --install --namespace gitlab-runner gitlab-runner-alpine \
  -f config-runner-alpine.yaml \
  --set serviceAccount.create=true \
  gitlab/gitlab-runner \
  --create-namespace

احصل على الرموز من واجهة GitLab (مشغّلات المجموعة/المشروع/المنشأة) أو من الأسرار التي يديرها المشغّل. تفضّل رموز المصادقة الحديثة للمشغّلات؛ رموز التسجيل قديمة وستُزال مع GitLab 18.لا تُلخّص أبدًا الرموز النشطة— قد تحتوي سكريبتات المختبر على رموز افتراضية يجب استبدالها محليًا.

6. التوسع التلقائي على مستويين (في الواقع أربعة)

"توسيع GitLab Runners تلقائياً على Kubernetes" ليس مفتاحاً واحداً. ضع هذه المقابض فوق بعضها:

  1. مرونة وحدات عمل الحاويات (Job pods)— مدمجة في مشغل Kubernetes. صفر مهام → صفر وحدات عمل مهام. هذا وحده يلغي معظم الهدر لكل مهمة على عناقيد مشتركة.
  2. المشغلconcurrentوعمليات نشر متعددة للمشغلات— افصل بين alpine و ubuntu (أو CPU والمُصنِّعين الأكبر) حتى لا تبقى سعة متخصصة خاملة لخلط غير مناسب.
  3. توسيع العناقيد/العُقَد تلقائياً— تضيف العُقَد الحاويات المعلقة؛ تغادر العُقَد الفارغة بعد الذروة المسائية.
  4. سياسة اختيارية واعية بالجدول الزمني— خفض حدود التوازي أو توسيع مجموعات العُقَد على تقويم ليالي/أيام عطلة كإجراء احتياطي إضافي فوق الانهيار الطبيعي للطلب.

القصة نفسها تنطبق على التوسع الضخم مع سعة أكبر: وفرِّد للصفوف العميقة، ثم أزل الموارد بنشاط حتى لا تشبه النصف الهادئ من الأسبوع النصف المزدحم في الفاتورة.

6.1 ملاحظة حول "خامل" بمعني GitLab Runner

يحافظ بعض المشغلات على عدد صغير من الآلات الخاملة ساخنة لامتصاص المهمة التالية دون تأخير بدء بارد. على Kubernetes، يكون بدء العمل البارد عادةً بإنشاء حاوية (ثوانٍ)، وليس تشغيل آلة افتراضية (دقائق). تفضّل ترك الحاويات تتجه للصفر وتحمل تأخيراً جدولياً قصيراً بدلاً من الاحتفاظ بقدرة ليلية فارغة "لحالة الطوارئ". إذا اضطررت لرفع أرضية صغيرة، فقم بتعديله واقع الاستدعاء — لا عاصفة اندماج الاثنين.

6.2 توفير وإلغاء التوفير ديناميكيًا من البداية إلى النهاية

تتبع مهمة خط أنابيب واحد:

  1. يقوم المطور بالضغط (Push)، ويُنشئ GitLab مهمة في قائمة الانتظار.
  2. يُطلب المهمة من قبل مدير الـ Runner ويطلب من API إنشاء Pod.
  3. إذا كان العنقود (Cluster) يعاني من نقص في CPU/الذاكرة العشوائية (RAM)، يضيف مقياس التلقائي عقدة (توفير).
  4. ينفذ الـ Pod السكريبت، يرفع الملفات الناتجة، ويخرج.
  5. يتم حذف الـ Pod؛ تعود الموارد إلى المجموعة (إلغاء التوفير على مستوى المهمة).
  6. عندما تجلس العديد من العقد فارغة بعد عتبة التقليل — وهو أمر شائع بعد المساء طوال عطلة نهاية الأسبوع — تغادر العقد (إلغاء التوفير على مستوى البنية التحتية).

هذا الحلقة الكاملة هي ما يقصده الفيديو بـ "Runners GitLab على نطاق ضخم" لتحقيق تحسين التكلفة: ليس مجرد علم (Flag) واحد متقن، بل دورة حياة المهمة + مرونة العنقود يعملان معًا.

7. نموذج التكلفة: حيث تظهر الوفورات الكبيرة بالدولار

كن دقيقًا. لا يجعل التوسع التلقائي عمليات البناء مجانية. إنه يمنعك من دفع أسعار الذروة خلال ساعات غير الذروة. تأتي الوفورات من مطابقة الإنفاق مع الطلب الحقيقي — النقاط الأربعة من الدليل المبسط، موسعة للمشغلين.

7.1 قم بالتوسع فقط عندما يعمل الناس (أو الروبوتات)

عندما يحل صباح مزدحم بعشرات خطوط الأنابيب، يُجدول Kubernetes العديد من Pods المهام بالتوازي حتى حدود التوازي وحدود العنقود. يظهر الإنتاجية عندما يكون ضغط الدمج حقيقيًا.

7.2 قلل الحجم بشدة عندما يختفي الطلب

عندما تنتهي المهام، تختفي الحاويات. مع توسيع العنقود تلقائيًا (أو مجموعة عقد بحجم مناسب)، تغادر العقد السحابية غير المستخدمة المجموعة. الليالي والأيام العطلية — وهي عادةً النوافذ الأكثر هدوءًا لفِرق المنتجات — هي أول سعة يجب أن تتوقف عن دفع ثمنها.

7.3 توقف عن إهدار CPU والذاكرة والتخزين

المواردآلات تشغيل افتراضية تعمل على مدار الساعةحاويات مهام Kubernetes + توسيع العقد تلقائيًا
CPUالنوى المحجوزة خاملة بينما الطابور فارغيتم الإفراج عنها عند خروج الحاويات؛ يمكن للعقد أن تتقلص
الذاكرةنظام تشغيل الوكيل + التنفيذيون خاملون مقيمون على مدار الساعة 24×7تعود الذاكرة مع كل حذف للحاوية
التخزينأقراص دافئة وطبقات صور على كل آلة افتراضيةمسودة مؤقتة افتراضيًا؛ تصبح التخزينات المشتركة خيارًا صريحًا ومحدد الحجم

على مدار شهر، تهيمن الساعات الهادئة على المؤقت. استعادة الليالي والأيام العطلية هي حيث تتراكمتوفيرات الدولار.

7.4 ادفع مقابل النتائج، لا مقابل الأثاث

لا تزال تدفع مقابل GitLab ولوحة تحكم رقيقة (مدير التشغيل الافتراضي + أساسيات العنقود). ما تتوقف عن دفع ثمنه هو مستودع من الكراسي الفارغة.

7.5 الحدس العملي (ليس معيارًا مصطنعًا)

افترض أن النهار يحتاج بشكل مستدام إلى ما يعادل 20 فتحة مشغّل نشطة، بينما الليل والأيام العطلية تحتاج 2. أسطول ثابت بحجم 20 يدفع ثمن 20 على مدار الساعة. حوض مرن يدفع ثمن ~20 خلال النهار و~2 (بما في ذلك مستوى التحكم) عندما يكون الهدوء. بالنسبة لكثير من فرق المنتجات، تشكل ساعات الهدوء نسبة كبيرة من الشهر — لذا فإن استردادها هو كيف تصبحكبيرةدون اختراع نسبة تسويقية. يضاعف المالية أسعار ساعة العقدة المحلية؛ وظيفة الهندسة المعمارية هي جعل الساعات الفارغة حقًا فارغة في حساب الفواتير.

تظهر وفورات التكلفة الكبيرة عندما لا يحدد ذروة يوم الاثنين فاتورة يوم الثلاثاء في الساعة 3 صباحًا — وعندما تبدو صمت يوم السبت أخيرًا هادئًا على الفاتورة أيضًا.

7.6 ما تدفعه عمدًا

  • مكونات سيرفر GitLab — حجمها للمستخدمين وتنسيق CI، وليس لمزرعة التجميع.
  • مدير Runner Deployment(s) — صغير مقارنة بمزارع الوظائف.
  • ذاكرات التخزين المؤقت المتعمدة (وكيل الاعتماديات، PVCs) — مفيدة، لكنها بحجم محدد؛ ذاكرات التخزين المؤقت ليست تخزينًا مجانيًا.
  • DinD ذو الامتيازات — مريح وأثقل؛ فكر في Kaniko/BuildKit عندما تكون الكثافة والعزل أكثر أهمية من الألفة.

8. خطوط الأنابيب CI/CD في الممارسة العملية

مع تشغيل العدّائين عبر الإنترنت، يُعرّف.gitlab-ci.ymlالمراحل والوظائف. يُجدّز GitLab؛ ويُحقّق Kubernetes العدّاء حاويات. حافظ على دقة خطوط الأنابيب فيما يتعلق بالتكلفة:

  • أخفِض السرعة سريعًا على lint/unit قبل بناء الصور الثقيلة.
  • استخدمrules/workflowحتى لا تتفرّع الفروع المسودة عبر مصفوفات كاملة.
  • اعتمد على التخزين المؤقت المشترك بمفاتيح واضحة بدل نمو القرص لكل آلة افتراضية دون حدود.
  • وسمّ الوظائف بالبركة المناسبة من العدّائين (alpine مقابل ubuntu، مصمّرات صغيرة مقابل كبيرة).
stages: [lint, test, build]

workflow:
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH

lint:
  stage: lint
  image: alpine:3.19
  script:
    - echo "cheap checks first"

test:
  stage: test
  tags: [kubernetes, alpine]
  script:
    - echo "unit tests"

build:
  stage: build
  tags: [kubernetes, dind]
  rules:
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH
  script:
    - echo "heavy image build only on default branch"

الفكرة الاقتصادية هي نفسها فكرة المنصة: لا جدّز أعمالًا مكلفة عندما كان فحصًا رخيصًا سيُفشلها، ولا تحافظ على العدّائين المتخصّصين دافئًا لوظائف لا تصل أبدًا يوم السبت.

9. ملاحظات الأمان والإيجار

تحسّن الحاويات المؤقتة النظافة (حالة أقلّ لاصقة) لكن DinD المُفضّل والـ RBAC على مستوى العنقود يمكن أن يوسّع نطاق الانفجار. الافتراضات العملية لمعظم الفرق:

  • شغّل حاويات الوظائف في مساحة مخصصة مع ResourceQuotas و LimitRanges.
  • اعتمد على البناء غير المُفضّل قدر الإمكان؛ عزّل عدّائين DinD خلف وسمّات محددة.
  • تجنّب تحميل بيانات اعتماد سحابية طويلة الأمد في كل وظيفة؛ حقّن رموزًا قصيرة الأمد لكل خط أنابيب.
  • معالج رموز تسجيل العدّائين كسرّيات — دوّرها عند مغادرة الأشخاص أو مشاركة المختبرات.
  • إذا شاركت عدة فرق عنقودًا، افصِل مديري العدّائين (وباختيار مجموعات العقد) حتى لا يبقّي جارٌ ضاغط كامل المزرعة ساخّنًا — واحفظ قصة التكلفة قابلةً للنسبة لكل فريق.

10. قابلية المراقبة التي تثبت الوفورات

لا يمكنك ادعاء الوفورات الليلية وال выходные دون النظر. راقب على الأقل:

انحراف / "يعمل على runner 3"شائعمخفض (عابر افتراضيًا)
تعقيد تشغيليأقل في البدايةأعلى (يُطلَب مهارات تجميع)

اختر VMs ثابتة فقط عندما يكون لديك طلب مسطح 24×7 حقيقي أو قيود تمنع التجميع. الجميع الآخرون مع خطوط أنابيب مدفوعة بالبشر ذات القمم المدفوعة يدفعون ضريبة الأثاث.

12. ما لا تفقده

التوسيع التلقائي لا يعني "لا تحكم". لا تزال تحدد التزامن، الصور المسموح بها، امتيازات DinD، سياسة الشبكة، ونطاق التسجيل. النقطة هي الحفاظ على هذه التحكيمات مع السماح للسعة غير المستخدمة بالتبخر — نفس الطمأنينة كما في القطعة بلغة بسيطة، الآن تُنفَّذ مع RBAC، المساحات، وإصدارات منفصلة للـ runners.

13. قائمة التحقق التشغيلية

  1. إصدارات مشغّل الرسم البياني/المخطط؛ قم بالترقية بوعي.
  2. دوّر رموز التشغيل؛ امسح رموز المختبر من أي سكريبت قبل النشر.
  3. مساحات أسماء منفصلة: نظام GitLab مقابل مهام التشغيل.
  4. راقبالقواريرالمعلقة — ارتفاع القوارير المعلقة يعني أن التوازي أو سعة العقد غير كافٍ في ذروة الحمل.
  5. راقبساعات العقد الفارغة— بقاء العقد فارغة طوال الليل يعني تأخير في تقليص الحجم أو حاجة لضبط سياسة المجموعة.
  6. حدّد مشغّلات الامتيازات إلى المهام التي تحتاجها فقط.
  7. احتفظ بنسخ احتياطية لـ GitLab بشكل مستقل عن مرونة تشغيلات التشغيل.
  8. راجع الفاتورة حسب ساعة الأسبوع بمجرد تشغيل CI المرن — يجب أن تنخفض الليالي والأيام العطل بشكل واضح.

14. من هذا المنشور موجه إليه

  • مهندسو المنصات و SREs الذين يطبقون GitLab CI على Kubernetes.
  • قادة DevOps الذين يستبدلون خوادم تشغيل افتراضية دائمة بـ Pods تنفيذية.
  • شركاء الهندسة والمالية الذين يحتاجون إلى أن يتصرف CI كخدمة تعتمد على الاستخدام، وليس أثاثًا.

15. وثائق GitLab الرسمية

هذه الصفحات هي المراجع القياسية لتوزيعات Helm وسلوك التوسع المذكور أعلاه. تفضّلها على المقالات المدوَّنة عند تغيير الإصدارات.

خادم GitLab على Kubernetes

  • قم بتثبيت مشغل GitLab— مسار تثبيت المشغل + Helm المستخدم في شرح التدريب.
  • مخططات GitLab Helm— توثيق مخطط المظلة.
  • قم بتثبيت GitLab باستخدام مخطط Helm— عند نشر GitLab عبر المخططات بدلاً من المشغل.
  • مخطط gitlab-runner الفرعي (مخطط GitLab)— runner مدمج بجانب GitLab في المخطط الرئيسي (مختلف عن مخطط runner المستقل).

مخطط GitLab Runner Helm

  • قم بتثبيت GitLab Runner باستخدام مخطط Helm—helm repo add gitlab، تثبيت/ترقية، ملاحظات مخطط OCI.
  • قم بتكوين GitLab Runner باستخدام مخطط Helm—concurrent، قوالب التكوين، RBAC، التخزين المؤقت، خيارات الصور.
  • مخطط gitlab-runnervalues.yaml— قيم افتراضية كاملة (بما في ذلك مسودات HPA الاختيارية).

Kubernetes executor وautoscaling

  • Kubernetes executor— job pods، helpers، services (مثل DinD)، resource requests، RBAC verbs.
  • إعداد autoscaling (Kubernetes executor / chart)— إيقاف pods،[runners.kubernetes.autoscaler]، سياسات الفترة (خامل ليلاً/في عطلة نهاية الأسبوع).
  • Autoscaling GitLab Runner— نموذج autoscaling عام (يتضمن أيضًا التوزيعية caching).
  • تخطيط وإدارة أسطول GitLab Runner— توسيع وتشغيل على مستوى الأسطول.
  • إعداد متقدم (config.toml)— أقسامconcurrentالعالمية وexecutor المدمجة في Helmrunners.config.

مهام CI، builds، وإعدادات runner في GitLab

  • إعداد runners في GitLab— التسجيل، tags، run-untagged، runners محمية.
  • استخدام Docker لبناء الصور في CI— DinD والبديلات (مُطبّق عندماprivileged/ خدمة Docker مفعّلة في runner values).

للتحكم في التكلفة ليلاً وفي عطلة نهاية الأسبوع، الجمع بين: (1) Kubernetes executor job pods التي تصل إلى صفر، (2) chartconcurrentوسياسات autoscalerمع off-peak، و(3) autoscaling cluster/node بحيث تغادر العقد الفارغة pool — كما هو موصوف في الأقسام 6–7.

16. العودة إلى الفيديو والمستودع

جلسة يوتيوب —GitLab الكامل في حوالي 20 دقيقة. توسيع نطاق GitLab Runner تلقائيًا باستخدام Kubernetes— يوضح GitLab على Kubernetes، والمُشغِّلات عبر Helm، وقصة التكلفة على نطاق واسع: توفير وإلغاء توفير البنية التحتية ديناميكيًا حتى لا تدفع أسعار الذروة في الليالي والأيام العطلات الخاملة. استخدم أمر البناء في هذا المستودعgitlab-runners-k3s-hyperscale-course.prompt.mdمع الوثائق الرسمية أعلاه كمصدر الحقيقة الموثق. للحصول على الإطار غير التقني لنفس الأفكار، انظرتوقف عن دفع تكاليف CI الخامل.

الخاتمة

لا يستضيف Kubernetes فقط مشغِّلات GitLab Runner. عند استخدامه بشكل صحيح، يغيّر اقتصاديات CI:توفير عند الطلب، إلغاء التوفير عند الخمول، استعادة CPU/الذاكرة/التخزين عندما يذهب البشر إلى المنزل. هذا هو نمط النطاق الواسع — متاح لأي فريق مستعد لتبادل الأسطول الدائم بصف من الحاويات.

ابدأ بالفيديو، أقم المشغِّل + المُشغِّل Helm في مختبر، فعّل توسيع نطاق العقد تلقائيًا، ثم افحص ما إذا كان السبت أخيرًا يبدو هادئًا في الفاتورة.
